exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Expected Value of a Sum of Random Variables

question.text:
The probability mass function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$
$f(x)$ $0.1$ $0.2$ $0.25$ $0.15$ $0.3$

$y$ $2$ $4$ $6$
$f(y)$ $0.25$ $0.5$ $0.25$

Find $\textrm E[5X+4Y].$
question.choice5: Impossible to determine because we don't know if $X$ and $Y$ are independent.
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm E[aX+bY] = a\textrm E[X] + b\textrm E[Y]. \]

First, let's find $\textrm E[X]$ and $\textrm E[Y].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space $S_x,$ then we have

\begin{align} \textrm E[X]&=\sum_{x\in S_x} x\cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &=0\cdot 0.1+1\cdot0.2+2\cdot 0.25+3\cdot 0.15+4\cdot 0.3\\[5pt] &=2.35. \end{align}

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space $S_y,$ then we have

\begin{align} \textrm E[Y]&=\sum_{y\in S_y} y\cdot f(y)\\[5pt] &=2\cdot 0.25+4\cdot0.5+6\cdot 0.25\\[5pt] &=4. \end{align}

Hence, we have \begin{align} \textrm E[5X+4Y]&=\textrm E[5X]+\textrm E[4Y]\\[5pt] &=5\textrm E[X]+4\textrm E[Y]\\[5pt] &=5\cdot 2.35+4\cdot 4\\[5pt] &=27.75. \end{align}

question.text:
The probability mass function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(x)$ $0.1$ $0.6$ $0.2$ $0.1$
$y$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$f(y)$ $0.5$ $0.3$ $0.2$

Find $\textrm E[3Y-X].$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm E[aX+bY] = a\textrm E[X] + b\textrm E[Y]. \]

First, let's find $\textrm E[X]$ and $\textrm E[Y].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space $S_x,$ then we have

\begin{align} \textrm E[X] &= \sum_{x\in S_x} x\cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &= 0 \cdot 0.1 + 1 \cdot 0.6 + 2 \cdot 0.2 + 3 \cdot 0.1\\[5pt] &= 1.3. \end{align}

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space $S_y,$ then we have

\begin{align} \textrm E[Y] &= \sum_{y\in S_y} y\cdot f(y)\\[5pt] &= 0 \cdot 0.5 + 1 \cdot 0.3 + 2 \cdot 0.2 \\[5pt] &= 0.7. \end{align}

Hence, we have \begin{align} \textrm E[3Y-X] &= \textrm E[3Y] + \textrm E[-X] \\[5pt] &= 3 \textrm E[Y] - \textrm E[X] \\[5pt] &= 3 \cdot 0.7 - 1.3\\[5pt] &= 0.8. \end{align}

question.text:
The probability mass function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

$x$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$
$f(x)$ $\dfrac{1}{6}$ $\dfrac{1}{3}$ $\dfrac{1}{6}$ $\dfrac{1}{3}$
$y$ $1$ $5$ $10$
$f(y)$ $\dfrac{5}{8}$ $\dfrac{1}{8}$ $\dfrac{1}{4}$

Find $\textrm E[4Y-3X].$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm E[aX+bY] = a\textrm E[X] + b\textrm E[Y]. \]

First, let's find $\textrm E[X]$ and $\textrm E[Y].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space $S_x,$ then we have

\begin{align} \textrm E[X] &= \sum_{x\in S_x} x\cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &= 1\cdot \dfrac{1}{6} + 2\cdot\dfrac{1}{3} + 3\cdot \dfrac{1}{6} + 4\cdot \dfrac{1}{3}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8}{3}. \end{align}

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space $S_y,$ then we have

\begin{align} \textrm E[Y] &= \sum_{y\in S_y} y\cdot f(y)\\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot \dfrac{5}{8} +5 \cdot\dfrac{1}{8}+ 10 \cdot \dfrac{1}{4}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{15}{4}. \end{align}

Hence, we have \begin{align} \textrm E[4Y-3X] &= \textrm E[4Y] + \textrm E[-3X] \\[5pt] &= 4\textrm E[Y] - 3\textrm E[X] \\[5pt] &= 4 \cdot \dfrac{15}{4} - 3 \cdot \dfrac{8}{3}\\[5pt] &= 7. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Expected Value of a Sum of Random Variables

question.text:
The probability mass function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

$x$ $-4$ $-2$ $2$ $4$
$f(x)$ $\dfrac{1}{6}$ $\dfrac{1}{3}$ $\dfrac{1}{3}$ $\dfrac{1}{6}$
$y$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(y)$ $\dfrac{1}{4}$ $\dfrac{1}{4}$ $\dfrac{1}{2}$

Find $\textrm E[10X+8Y].$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm E[aX+bY] = a\textrm E[X] + b\textrm E[Y]. \]

First, let's find $\textrm E[X]$ and $\textrm E[Y].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space $S_x,$ then we have

\begin{align} \textrm E[X] &= \sum_{x\in S_x} x\cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &= -4\cdot \dfrac{1}{6} - 2\cdot\dfrac{1}{3} + 2\cdot \dfrac{1}{3} + 4\cdot \dfrac{1}{6}\\[5pt] &= 0. \end{align}

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space $S_y,$ then we have

\begin{align} \textrm E[Y] &= \sum_{y\in S_y} y\cdot f(y)\\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot \dfrac{1}{4} + 2 \cdot\dfrac{1}{4}+ 3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{4}. \end{align}

Hence, we have \begin{align} \textrm E[10X+8Y] &= \textrm E[10X] + \textrm E[8Y] \\[5pt] &= 10 \textrm E[X] + 8\textrm E[Y] \\[5pt] &= 10 \cdot 0 + 8 \cdot \dfrac{9}{4}\\[5pt] &= 18. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Expected Value of a Sum of Random Variables in Context

question.text:
In a factory, two machines independently produce the same product. The random variable $X$ represents the number of rejects per day of the first machine, and the random variable $Y$ is the number of rejects per day on another machine. The probability distributions of $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(x)$ $0.1$ $0.6$ $0.2$ $0.1$
$y$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$f(y)$ $0.5$ $0.3$ $0.2$

Calculate the expected number of items per day that the factory rejects.
question.explanation:
We need to calculate $\textrm E[X+Y].$

Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm E[aX+bY] = a\textrm E[X] + b\textrm E[Y]. \]

The expected values of $X$ and $Y$ are calculated as follows: \begin{align} \textrm E[X]&=0\cdot 0.1+1\cdot 0.6+2\cdot 0.2+3\cdot 0.1=1.3\\[5pt] \textrm E[Y]&=0\cdot 0.5+1\cdot 0.3+2\cdot 0.2=0.7 \end{align}

Hence, we get

$$ \textrm E[X+Y]=\textrm E[X]+\textrm E[Y]=1.3+0.7=2. $$

example.title: Finding the Expected Value of a Sum of Random Variables in Context

question.text: Michael has two card decks. One of them contains five cards, the cards are labeled with numbers $0,$ $2,$ $4,$ $6,$ and $8$, and the other deck contains four cards, labeled with numbers $1,$ $3,$ $5,$ and $7.$ From each of the two decks one card is randomly drawn. What is the expected value of the sum of the numbers of the cards?
question.explanation:
We need to calculate $\textrm E[X+Y].$

Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm E[aX+bY] = a\textrm E[X] + b\textrm E[Y]. \]

Let the random variable $X$ be the number of the card drawn from the first deck, and the random variable $Y$ be the number of the card drawn from the second deck.

The expected values of $X$ and $Y$ are calculated as follows: \begin{align} \textrm E[X]&= 0\cdot \dfrac{1}{5}+2\cdot \dfrac{1}{5}+4\cdot \dfrac{1}{5} +6\cdot \dfrac{1}{5}+8\cdot \dfrac{1}{5} =4\\[5pt] \textrm E[Y]&= 1\cdot \dfrac{1}{4}+3\cdot \dfrac{1}{4}+5\cdot \dfrac{1}{4} +7\cdot \dfrac{1}{4} = 4 \end{align}

Hence, we get

\[ \textrm E[X+Y]=\textrm E[X]+\textrm E[Y]= 4+4 = 8. \]

question.text:
In a cafe, there is a kettle and a microwave oven. The random variable $X$ represents the number of breakdowns per year of the kettle, and the random variable $Y$ is the number of breakdowns per year of the microwave oven. The probability distributions of $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(x)$ $0.2$ $0.4$ $0.3$ $0.1$
$y$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$f(y)$ $0.6$ $0.3$ $0.1$

Calculate the expected number of breakdowns per year of both appliances.
question.explanation:
We need to calculate $\textrm E[X+Y].$

Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm E[aX+bY] = a\textrm E[X] + b\textrm E[Y]. \]

The expected values of $X$ and $Y$ are calculated as follows: \begin{align} \textrm E[X] &=0\cdot 0.2+1\cdot 0.4+2\cdot 0.3+3\cdot 0.1=1.3\\[5pt] \textrm E[Y] &=0\cdot 0.6+1\cdot 0.3+2\cdot 0.1=0.5 \end{align}

Hence, we get

\[ \textrm E[X+Y]=\textrm E[X]+\textrm E[Y]=1.3+0.5=1.8. \]

question.text:
Anna has two spinners. The first has three sections labeled $1, 2, 3,$ and the second has four sections labeled $0, 2, 4, 8.$ The random variable $X$ represents the number obtained by the first spinner, and $Y$ is the number obtained by the second spinner. Each of the two spinners is rolled once. What is the expected value of the sum of the outcomes?

$x$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(x)$ $0.4$ $0.4$ $0.2$
$y$ $0$ $2$ $4$ $8$
$f(y)$ $0.5$ $0.3$ $0.1$ $0.1$
question.explanation:
We need to calculate $\textrm E[X+Y].$

Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm E[aX+bY] = a\textrm E[X] + b\textrm E[Y]. \]

The expected values of $X$ and $Y$ are calculated as follows: \begin{align} \textrm E[X]&= 1\cdot 0.4 + 2\cdot 0.4 + 3\cdot 0.2 = 1.8 \\[5pt] \textrm E[Y]&= 0\cdot 0.5 + 2\cdot 0.3 + 4\cdot 0.1 + 8\cdot 0.1 = 1.8 \end{align}

Hence, we get

\[ \textrm E[X+Y]=\textrm E[X]+\textrm E[Y]= 1.8 + 1.8 = 3.6. \]

example.title: Finding the Expected Value of a Sum of Random Variables in Context

question.text:
Marcus has two spinners. The first of them has three sections labeled $1, 2, 3,$ and the second has four sections labeled $0, 2, 4, 8.$ The random variable $X$ represents the number obtained on a typical throw of the first spinner, and $Y$ is the number obtained on a typical throw of the second spinner. The first spinner is rolled $10$ times, and the second spinner is rolled $5$ times. What is the expected value of the sum of all outcomes?

$x$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(x)$ $0.4$ $0.4$ $0.2$
$y$ $0$ $2$ $4$ $8$
$f(y)$ $0.5$ $0.3$ $0.1$ $0.1$
question.explanation:
Let $X_i$ be the $i$th score obtained from the first spinner, and let $Y_j$ be the $j$th score obtained from the second spinner. Then, we need to calculate

\[ \textrm E\left[ \sum_{i=1}^{10} X_i + \sum_{j=1}^5 Y_j \right]. \]

Using the properties of expected value, we have

\begin{align*} \textrm E\left[ \sum_{i=1}^{10} X_i + \sum_{j=1}^5 Y_j \right] &=\sum_{i=1}^{10} \textrm{E}[X_i] + \sum_{j=1}^5 \textrm E[Y_j] \\[5pt] &=10\textrm E[X] + 5\textrm E[Y], \end{align*}

where the last equality above is true because $\textrm E[X_i] = \textrm E[X]$ and $\textrm E[Y_j] = \textrm E[Y]$ for all $1\leq i \leq 10,\: 1\leq j\leq 5.$

The expected values of $X$ and $Y$ are calculated as follows: \begin{align} \textrm E[X]&= 1\cdot 0.4 + 2\cdot 0.4 + 3\cdot 0.2 = 1.8 \\[5pt] \textrm E[Y]&= 0\cdot 0.5 + 2\cdot 0.3 + 4\cdot 0.1 + 8\cdot 0.1 = 1.8 \end{align}

Hence, we get

\[ \textrm E[10X+5Y]=10\textrm E[X]+5\textrm E[Y]= 10 \cdot 1.8 + 5 \cdot 1.8 = 27. \]

\[ \textrm E[X\cdot Y]=\textrm E[X]\cdot \textrm E[Y] \]
